steps.message:
Done. Baseline was green (2 tests); the new suite is green with 7 tests, and `verify_mutations.sh` exits 0 — every one of the five original mutations is now killed. Production code and DiscountRulesTests.cs are untouched.

Verified survivors and the tests that close them:

1. Whitespace code (guard). `string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(code)` mutated to `IsNullOrEmpty(code)` survives the original suite. Added `Apply(50m, "   ")` returns 50m — under the mutant a whitespace code falls through to the switch and throws, so this fails red.

2. Case-insensitive matching. `code.ToUpperInvariant() switch` mutated to `code switch` survives. Added `Apply(100m, "save10")` returns 90m — the mutant no longer normalizes case, hits the `_` arm and throws.

3. FLAT5 floor below five dollars (boundary / return-value). `Math.Max(0m, subtotal - 5m)` mutated to `subtotal - 5m` survives. Added `Apply(3m, "FLAT5")` returns 0m, not -2m, pinning the clamp.

4. Negative-subtotal guard (boundary). `subtotal < 0` mutated to `subtotal < -1m` survives. Added `Assert.Throws<ArgumentOutOfRangeException>(() => Apply(-1m, null))` — the mutant lets -1 through.

5. Unknown-code rejection (exception). `_ => throw new ArgumentException(...)` mutated to `_ => subtotal` survives. Added `Assert.Throws<ArgumentException>(() => Apply(50m, "BOGUS"))`.

I deliberately did not duplicate the null-code passthrough or the ordinary uppercase SAVE10 case the existing suite already protects — that would add count without value. Five added facts plus the two existing tests is seven, within the eight-test budget.
